name: India: Kashmir, Manipur and the Maoist belt

status.en: 357 armed incidents reported in the past seven days, most of them in Delhi, Mumbai and Hyderabad.
status.nb: 357 væpnede hendelser meldt de siste sju dagene, flest i Delhi, Mumbai og Hyderabad.

summary.en: Security forces conducted an anti-fidayeen drill at a railway station in Kulgam, while a landmine blast on the LoC in Poonch killed four terrorists, including a LeT commander, according to a news report. In South Kashmir a man was injured in a bear attack and another man suffered injuries in a separate bear incident. Manipur saw the Makui Village Authority condemn firing and demand immediate security intervention, and protests continued with supporters marching to a BJP headquarters and staging a home sit-in. The conflict produced 437 battle-related deaths in 2024, according to UCDP.
summary.nb: Sikkerhetsstyrker gjennomførte en anti-fidayeen-øvelse på en jernbanestasjon i Kulgam, mens en landmineeksplosjon på LoC i Poonch drepte fire terrorister, inkludert en LeT-kommandør, ifølge en nyhetsrapport. I Sør-Kashmir ble en mann skadet i et bjørneangrep og en annen mann pådro seg skader i en separat bjørnehendelse. I Manipur fordømte Makui Village Authority skytingen og krevde umiddelbar sikkerhetsintervensjon, og protestene fortsatte med støttespillere som marsjerte til et BJP-hovedkvarter og holdt en hus-sitt-in. Konflikten førte til 437 kamprelaterte dødsfall i 2024, ifølge UCDP.

background.title: Kashmir conflict
background.extract: The Kashmir conflict is a territorial conflict over the Kashmir region, primarily between India and Pakistan, and also between China and India in the northeastern portion of the region. The conflict started after the partition of India in 1947 as both India and Pakistan claimed the entirety of the former princely state of Jammu and Kashmir. It is a dispute over the region that escalated into three wars between India and Pakistan and several other armed skirmishes. India controls approximately 55% of the land area of the region that includes Jammu, the Kashmir Valley, most of Ladakh, the Siachen Glacier, and 70% of its population; Pakistan controls approximately 30% of the land area that includes Azad Kashmir and Gilgit-Baltistan; and China controls the remaining 15% of the land area that includes the Aksai Chin region, the mostly uninhabited Trans-Karakoram Tract, and part of the Demchok sector.
